title: Semantic Blindness: 500,000 Sensors Confused an LLM - Raahul Singh & Vanč Levstik, Phaidra
talk_summary: Phaidra's agents query data-center equipment by having an LLM plan a structured search (scope subtree + filters + name patterns) and a deterministic resolver do indexing/set operations, instead of stuffing 500k sensor names into context or relying on vector search. They report flat ~9k tokens/query and 100% correctness from 64 to 460k GPUs, versus 80%→30% correctness and 116M tokens per validation pass for the naive approach.

takeaways.what_they_do: The LLM emits structured output (what to collect, scope subtree, filters, or name patterns); a deterministic backend does indexing, set operations, and exact matching, so the model never scans the full name/entity list.
takeaways.evidence_quote: LLMs are good for planning but not good for searching.
takeaways.numbers: ~9,000 tokens/query flat at 64 and 460,000 GPUs; 390k vs 116M tokens per validation pass (~300x fewer)

takeaways.technique: Summarize by tree depth, not instance count
takeaways.what_they_do: They describe only root-to-leaf paths of the hierarchy, so a 64-GPU and a 460k-GPU plant produce roughly the same-size summary in context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: 64 GPU system and a 460,000 GPU system produce roughly the same size of summaries.
takeaways.numbers: Same summary size at 64 vs 460,000 GPUs

takeaways.what_they_do: They pre-build index subsets (e.g., all GPUs in data hall 11) and answer queries by intersecting pre-indexed sets with filter results, guaranteeing exact recall.
takeaways.numbers: 100% correctness on 66 cases across 6 real production systems, zero failures

takeaways.technique: Two-to-three-step plan instead of agentic loop
takeaways.what_they_do: End-to-end query is planner LLM → deterministic resolver → answer, replacing a multi-step agentic loop that re-runs over and over.
takeaways.evidence_quote: All of this is a two or three-step process instead of a multi-step agentic loop, which can keep on running over and over again.

takeaways.technique: Head-to-head eval, same model/data, 3 runs per case
takeaways.what_they_do: Before shipping, they benchmarked new vs old system with identical model and data, three runs per case, on synthetic plus 66 real production cases across 6 systems.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We measured the new system head-to-head against the old ones with same LLM model, same data, and we did three runs per case just to make sure.
takeaways.numbers: Old: 80% at 64 GPUs → ~30% at 460k; new: 100%; 66 real cases, 0 failures

takeaways.technique: Push structured work into code, keep judgment in the LLM
takeaways.what_they_do: They explicitly classify work: LLM for parsing ambiguous requests, deciding where/what to look for, and final synthesis; deterministic code for retrieval, counting, dedup, and anything needing reproducibility.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If you can write down the structure or the rules, it's a 1.0 job.
